title: McCurdy, Picou and the flute-part story told again
summary: Asked about McCurdy, Laurent repeats the Baquet account, set on an out-of-town job, and recalls playing duets with Picou in a backyard.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: I was going to ask, somebody told me that McCurdy, that Shorty McCurdy played that high society the first time, but you don't think that.
Well, I'm giving to you the way I got. They said that was the voice and that's why the variation came from.
France holds up a flute copy.
To be played that night. It had to be played that night. They didn't have no copy for the Clarenters. You don't remember what job that was. No, that was way from here.

out of town. Around, I believe it was somewhere around Philadelphia. Yeah, I believe it was in Philadelphia somewhere that happened. Right on the job they transposed it and the clarinet played that night, played the variation. That's where they got the variation from. But later on, like I said, they brought it up here. But me, I know part of the fact that Pico didn't. Because I heard Pico play all these days, I was a kid coming up under him. We used to sit down together at one of his lady friends' house. In the backyard, two clarinets, Pico on one and me on one, and played together. I'd lead off. I'd pick up my lead off for him. He'd bury it. And he'd lead off and I'd play it. Just us two.
